name: Multi-asset income ETF allocation
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Diversified Income Sources
caseLead: Multi-asset income funds combine distributions from bonds, dividend-paying equities and listed property, with each source exposed to different risks. Combining these income streams can reduce dependence on any single asset class, although inflation and interest rate changes can still affect several holdings at once.
caseRest: Diversification can weaken when bonds, shares and property fall together, particularly during periods of rising inflation and interest rates. In 2022 higher inflation and rising policy rates lowered the value of every income source together. Funds also charge management fees and can trade below net asset value in a sell-off, so returns can fall short of the income collected.
figNote: Each card shows the change in the S&P 500 over the episode, measured from its high before the event to its low, or from its low to its high in a rally. It is a simple measure of how severe the move in the equity market was, so readers can compare how a mix of income funds behaved against it.

events.title: US downgrade lifts bonds and weakens equities
events.text: The S&P 500 fell about 19% from April to October 2011 after the US credit rating downgrade, while Treasury yields fell and bond prices rose. Results were mixed because gains on bond funds offset part of the fall in dividend shares and listed property.

events.title: Taper signal weakens bonds and property
events.text: The Federal Reserve signalled in May 2013 that it would slow bond purchases, and the S&P 500 fell about 6% in the following month as bond yields rose. The strategy lost because bonds, utilities and listed property fell together, so diversification gave little protection.

events.title: Tighter policy and tariffs weigh on equities
events.text: The S&P 500 fell about 20% from September to December 2018 as the Federal Reserve raised rates and US-China tariffs weighed on growth. Results were mixed because bonds gained as equities fell, which cushioned the loss from dividend and property funds.

events.title: Covid sell-off hits all income sources
events.text: The S&P 500 fell about 34% in five weeks to 23 March 2020, and credit and property funds fell alongside equities as investors sold to raise cash. The strategy lost because most of its income sources fell together while dividends were cut.

events.title: Inflation pushes bonds and equities lower together
events.text: The S&P 500 fell about 25% from January to October 2022 as the Federal Reserve raised rates to control inflation, while bond prices fell as well. The strategy lost because the bond holdings that normally offset equity losses fell at the same time.

events.title: Fed signals cuts and bonds rally
events.text: The S&P 500 rose about 16% from late October to the end of 2023 after the Federal Reserve signalled rate cuts, and bond yields fell sharply. The strategy gained because bond, dividend and property funds all rose together.

instrument: ETFs holding bonds, dividend shares and listed property; rebalanced quarterly
rules: Income funds selected on yield, credit quality and fees; no fund above 25%; weights shifted towards bonds when equity volatility rises
costs: Fund expense ratios, estimated bid-ask spreads and commissions deducted at each rebalance
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from diversified income to volatility control

legs.purpose: Earns coupon income and cushions equity falls

legs.position: Investment grade and high yield credit ETFs

entry: Funds with yield above the five-year average and an expense ratio below 0.4%
size: Set to an 8% annualised volatility target; no fund above 25%
exit: Rebalanced quarterly, or when an asset class drifts 5 points from its weight
stop: Equity and property weights halved if the portfolio falls 12% from its high
marketWatch: Rehyn monitors the yield on each income source against government bonds, the correlation between share and bond returns, and credit spreads, because these show how well the mix is diversified. Central bank meetings, inflation releases and trade policy announcements are the events that most often move all three sources together. If bond and equity returns become more correlated, the protection from diversification would weaken.

favourable.heading: Falling yields and rate cuts
favourable.text: Falling yields favour the strategy because bond prices rise while dividend shares and property benefit from lower financing costs. From October to December 2023 a fall in Treasury yields lifted bonds, dividend funds and listed property together.

favourable.heading: Safe haven demand in sell-offs
favourable.text: Safe haven demand favours the strategy because bond prices rise when equities fall, which offsets part of the loss from dividend shares and property. During the December 2018 sell-off, Treasury prices rose while the S&P 500 fell about 20%.

favourable.heading: Stable inflation and growth
favourable.text: Stable inflation and growth favour the strategy because coupons and dividends continue while the prices of each income source change little. Between 2012 and 2019 US inflation stayed close to 2% and income funds delivered steady yields.

adverse.heading: Rising inflation and policy rates
adverse.text: Rising inflation hurts the strategy because higher yields reduce bond prices and the value of dividend shares and property at the same time. In 2022 the S&P 500 fell about 25% while the 10-year Treasury yield rose about 235 basis points, which removed the usual offset.

adverse.heading: Forced selling in a liquidity crisis
adverse.text: A scramble for cash hurts the strategy because investors sell liquid funds first, which pushes down bond, credit and property funds together. In March 2020 credit and property funds fell alongside equities, and many bond funds traded below the value of their holdings.

adverse.heading: Dividend cuts and credit defaults
adverse.text: Rising defaults hurt the strategy because companies cut dividends, bond issuers miss payments and property owners lose rent at the same time. In 2020 many companies in energy, travel and retail suspended dividends, which reduced income from the equity and property funds.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's peak-to-trough drawdown during each event, measured from its value just before the event to its lowest point using the default backtest parameters above. Each event window runs from the last market high before the shock to the market low.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects moves in global share prices, bond yields and credit spreads, which are then applied to the strategy's current fund weights.
